result.summary: Both N slots pass the first audit. Slot a (volume-return interaction) gets novelty 4 and soundness 3. I struck seed 8 because it uses raw returns that are not scaled by volatility, so the signal grows with volatility. The table separately strikes seeds 6, 9 and 12 for reversal |ρ| ≥ 0.5, which leaves 9 seeds. Slot a's soundness stays at 3 for two reasons: the CGW/LMSW evidence is about a 1–2 day reversal, not a 20–60 day ranking, and the minute-level seeds pick up the open/close U-shape in turnover rather than abnormal volume. Slot b (skewness/lottery) gets novelty 4 and soundness 4. I struck seed 11 (max/std, which still has residual |ρ| 0.53 with the head, so it is mostly the head again) and seed 10 (a one-sided right-tail ratio that reflects tick size and liquidity). The table also strikes seed 14, which leaves 11 seeds. The R group passes with soundness 3, and the parts it removes really are bad: the wrapper adds only +0.02 in the ablation and sits near the float32 limits, and the residual |ρ| of 0.87 between LFC−LFS and the head shows the head is really trading low nominal price. Three variants have problems. Variants 4 and 6 use log of the back-adjusted Close, which is not the nominal price (residual |ρ| 0.30 and size 0.42), so if they win they would be added to the library instead of replacing the head. Variant 9 (float ratio) does not remove a bad part and would wrongly take the replacement route. Variants 1, 2, 7 and 8 repeat the diagnostics the ablation already ran. If there is a rewrite, the R group should keep only variants 3 and 5.
